payload.text: Fixture race found at Utilz (their issue 0042, relayed 2026-09-20): a test fixture built with cp -a of a LIVE checkout, .git included, is not an atomic walk. A commit landing mid-copy gives a fixture whose .git carries files its worktree lacks, so git add -A stages deletions and an append-only guard refuses them -- which reads like data loss in the event store and is not. Their fix is ordering: copy .git FIRST and the worktree SECOND, so any tear stages as additions. MEASURED FOR DEVBIN, not assumed: devbin is not exposed. Its three recursive copies (tests/lib/source_fixtures.bash:41-42, tests/lib/test_helper.bash:844) take lib/ and bin/.devbin only, never .git and never the checkout root, and mkdevsrc runs git init plus one commit INSIDE the fixture after the bytes are there, so no pre-existing history can be copied at a different instant from the worktree. Keep this in mind for any future devbin fixture that copies a checkout.
